title: The First Step With An Out-Of-Control Class
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that the first move with an out-of-control class isn't to teach the classroom management plan, since rules land on deaf ears amid chaos, but to remove excitability from the room entirely. He describes a technique of embodying total physical and mental calm, achieved beforehand through stillness or meditation and sustained through slow breathing, gentle eye contact, and unhurried movement, arguing this calm energy gradually spreads to students. The article details specific behaviors to avoid during this phase, including threats, demands, or visible frustration, while recommending simple compliance requests, physical stretching activities, and patient repetition if needed. He frames this as one of SCM's most tested strategies precisely because it works regardless of how severe a class's dysfunction has become. The piece closes by describing this calm-first phase as the necessary precondition before a management plan can actually be introduced and take hold.
points: With an out-of-control class, teaching the classroom management plan first fails; the necessary first step is removing excitability from the room.
A teacher's own embodied calm, cultivated beforehand through stillness or meditation, is described as capable of gradually spreading to an entire agitated class.
Slow breathing, gentle eye contact, and unhurried movement are specific tools for projecting calm energy to students during this phase.
Threats, demands, and visible frustration should be avoided entirely during this calming phase; simple compliance requests and repetition are preferred.
Physical stretching activities can help settle a restless class and redirect their energy toward following instructions.
quotes: With an out-of-control class, bringing up rules right away will fall on deaf ears. No, the first step after losing control or taking over an unruly class is to remove excitability .
The culture is broken and can only heal when restlessness, tension, and agitation are removed. Only then can you introduce your classroom management plan and get a handle on misbehavior.
It’s to become so calm yourself that your peaceful energy spreads to every student in the class. I know it sounds new-agey, but it’s effective.

By your presence alone you’re pulling your students into your corner, on your side, and within your sphere of influence. Your calm likability will give you just enough space to be heard and listened to.
Build connection. Establish likability. Bring in fresh oxygen, a new vibe, and a common, more peaceful wavelength. Breathe in and out. Smile.
